props.name: The Rusty Flagon
props.descriptor: A well-worn tavern where travelers and locals share ale and secrets.

props.name: Market Square
props.descriptor: The beating heart of commerce, loud with haggling and rumor.

props.name: Guard Barracks
props.descriptor: The disciplined quarters of the city guard, smelling of iron and duty.

props.name: The Chapel
props.descriptor: A soot-stained stone chapel; the one place all factions leave alone.

props.name: The Forge
props.descriptor: A smoky workshop on Forge Row where iron is shaped into arms and tools.

props.name: Temple of the Unnamed
props.descriptor: A soot-stained stone temple; the one place all factions leave unwatched.

props.name: The Docks
props.descriptor: A salt-worn harbour district where manifests lie and crates move at night.

props.name: North Gate
props.descriptor: The fortified northern entry to the city — a strategic chokepoint under guard scrutiny.

props.name: Merchants Guild
props.description: Controls the flow of trade through the city.

props.name: City Guard
props.description: Enforces the law and defends the city walls.

props.name: Thieves Guild
props.description: A shadow organization that lives in the cracks of the city.

props.name: Iron Legion
props.description: The northern army that crossed the border at the start of the war.

props.name: Crown Loyalists
props.description: Agents of the distant crown, brokering treaties and tracking loyalties in the city.

props.name: Dockside Smugglers
props.description: A clandestine ring that profits from the war by moving contraband through the harbor.

props.voice_descriptor: Warm, observant. Cautious about politics — never says more than she needs to. Frames hard news as rumour or second-hand. Invites the listener to share what they know in return.
props.biography: Runs the Rusty Flagon with an even hand and a sharp ear.
props.name: Mira

props.voice_descriptor: Measured and precise. Every statement is a negotiation — he gives only what serves him. Refers to value, leverage, and risk. Distrusts sentiment.
props.biography: A veteran spice trader who knows every coin's worth and every man's price.
props.name: Aldric

props.voice_descriptor: Clipped military diction. Direct. Names the enemy without emotion or hesitation. No hedging, no qualifiers. Every sentence lands like a report to a superior officer.
props.biography: Commands the city watch with iron discipline and growing dread.
props.name: Captain Sorn

props.voice_descriptor: Light, deflective. Turns every question into a joke or a counter-question. Never volunteers information — makes you earn it. Laughs easily; means very little of it.
props.biography: Moves stolen goods with a smile and a story, always one step ahead.
props.name: Lira

props.voice_descriptor: Rambling. Mixes current rumour with personal memories from decades ago. Speaks with complete confidence even about details he has wrong. Never hedges.
props.biography: A retired courier who has seen three wars and remembers every one.
props.name: Old Henryk

props.voice_descriptor: Friendly and light, but vague when asked directly. Deflects with chores and small talk.
props.biography: Mira's assistant, quick with a cloth and quicker with her ears.
props.name: Sera

props.voice_descriptor: Blunt and literal. Trusts his officers. Uncomfortable with ambiguity.
props.biography: A rank-and-file soldier who follows orders and tries not to think too hard.
props.name: Harwick

props.voice_descriptor: Evasive, fast-talking. Denies everything. Pretends to be younger and more innocent than she is.
props.biography: A young guild runner who moves between tables and pockets without anyone noticing.
props.name: Nel

props.voice_descriptor: Gruff and straightforward. Every complaint is delivered as a statement of fact. Loyal to the guard grudgingly — the contract feeds him, but the tithes sting. Does not embellish; does not speculate.
props.biography: Supplies the guard with arms and repairs; resents every tithe they skim from his forge.
props.name: Bren

props.voice_descriptor: Composed and unhurried. Asks questions more than she answers them. Speaks in measured phrases, never raising her voice. Treats every secret as a burden she accepts willingly.
props.biography: The moral counterweight of the city; hears confessions from every faction and holds them all.
props.name: Nessa

props.voice_descriptor: Businesslike and evasive in equal measure. Quotes prices before he quotes opinions. Pauses before sensitive answers, as though recalculating risk. Claims everything is above board; means none of it.
props.biography: Controls the loading manifests; every off-book shipment passes through his ledger — or doesn't.
props.name: Dorn

props.voice_descriptor: Precise and economical. Each word is selected; none are wasted. Implies more than he states. Asks clarifying questions as a form of pressure. Never reveals how much he already knows.
props.biography: The crown's eyes in the city; brokers treaties and oaths on behalf of a king most have forgotten.
props.name: Vex

props.voice_descriptor: Cheerful on the surface; careful underneath. Uses botanical metaphors as deflection. Generous with common remedies, tight with rare ones. Never admits a customer's true purpose; that would be rude.
props.biography: Sells remedies at market — and something stronger to those who know how to ask.
props.name: Tilda

props.voice_descriptor: Quiet and watchful. Keeps his back to the wall and his answers short. Changes the subject when the war comes up. Laughs too quickly when nervous. War made him personal — every casualty has a name in his head.
props.biography: A soldier who walked away from the Iron Legion's advance; hiding in plain sight behind a cup.
props.name: Garrick

props.content: The guard takes a third of my contract pay as 'protection' — protection from themselves.
A city that cannot arm its own soldiers is a city already lost.

props.description: Renegotiate the forge contract before the war pushes iron prices beyond what the guard will pay.

props.content: The morning the guard captain walked in and increased the tithe. He did not ask.
Forging the sword that the last guard captain wore to his death. I wondered if the blade held.
He has been shaving the steel alloy ratios for six months — the guard's new swords are weaker than reported.
Every faction claims righteousness. None of them has sat with the dying to test that claim.
Confession is not absolution — but it is the only honest accounting most people ever give.

props.description: Keep the temple neutral so the wounded from both sides can be brought here without fear.

props.content: The night a guild enforcer and a city guard both bled on the same floor and refused to look at each other.
A merchant who confessed to arson and went home lighter. I lit a candle for those who lost the warehouse.
She knows who set the market fire and has not told the guard — the confession was genuine.
The manifest is a fiction — the real ledger lives in my head and nowhere else.
Lira moves more product through this port than the merchants guild does. That is a fact worth knowing.

props.description: Keep the smuggling routes open long enough to make one last large shipment before the war closes the docks.

props.content: The night I let a crate of stolen guard armor through without inspecting it. Lira paid triple the usual.
The morning the harbour authority showed up unannounced. I had the false manifests ready in thirty seconds.
He has been running the smuggling operation that Lira fronts — she thinks she runs it; she does not.
The city's factions are negotiating with each other every day. Most of them do not realize it.
A signed treaty is worth nothing without leverage behind it — the crown learned that the hard way.

props.description: Broker a non-aggression accord between the city guard and the merchants before the Iron Legion makes it irrelevant.

props.content: Watching a peace negotiation collapse over a single clause no one would reword. Both sides lost more than they would have given.
The day I was assigned to this city — a posting no one else wanted. I have been here long enough to know why.
He reports to the crown but has stopped forwarding certain intelligence — enough to make himself indispensable to both sides.
Plants do not lie. People always do. That is why I prefer plants.
The guild asked me to poison someone once. I said no. They have not asked again.

props.description: Find a reliable supply of northwood bark before the war cuts the trade routes — it is the only analgesic that works.

props.content: The day a guild contact brought me a herb I had never seen. I grew it; I sold what it produced quietly.
Treating a city guard's wound after a market brawl. He paid in coin and never asked what was in the poultice.
She has a cultivated batch of a controlled herb that the guild does not know about — her private insurance.
The Iron Legion does not take prisoners. I walked away because I saw what they do to towns that resist.
Everyone in this city is going to find out what the war really looks like. I already know.

props.description: Stay alive and invisible long enough to decide whether to warn the city or simply leave it.

props.content: The village we burned on the march. The officer called it a tactical necessity. I called it something else.
Mira hid me in the cellar the first night. She did not ask questions. That is the only kindness I remember.
He knows the Iron Legion's intended route through the city — information the guard captain would kill for.
The war will come here eventually — I have seen it before.
People reveal their true nature after the second drink.

props.description: Keep the Rusty Flagon a neutral ground where all factions are welcome.

props.content: The night a deserter begged at my door in the rain. I hid him in the cellar for a week.
The last time the city went to war — half my regulars never came back.
A stranger came in asking about the northern war. Nervous eyes, too many questions. I told them what little I knew.
She hid a deserter from the city guard last winter.
The guild protects those who pay their dues — and devours those who don't.
Thieves are a plague on honest commerce and should be hanged.

props.description: Corner the northern spice trade before the war closes the roads.
Expose the guild spy who has been skimming from the market accounts.

props.content: The night the south warehouse burned. I saw the guild master watching from across the street.
The day I signed my first guild contract — I did not read it carefully enough.
He has been skimming a tenth from his own guild tithe for two years.
The thieves guild is planning something large — the signs are all there.
The city walls have never been in worse repair. One hard winter could break us.

props.description: Catch Lira in a crime significant enough to break the guild's protection racket.

props.content: The morning I found the gate sergeant's bribe money hidden in his boot. I said nothing.
The day I was promoted to captain — my predecessor disappeared the same week.
He knows the name of the merchant who bribed the gate sergeant and has done nothing.
Every guard has a price — you just have to find the right currency.
Aldric's ledger holds enough guild secrets to bury half the market.

props.description: Get that ledger from Aldric before he realizes what it proves.

props.content: The night I moved a crate of stolen army supplies through the market. No one asked questions.
The first time I was caught — I was twelve, and the merchant let me go. I never forgot.
She is currently fencing a shipment of stolen city guard armor.
War changes everything about a place — the smell of fear never leaves.
Young captains always underestimate the thieves until it is too late.

props.description: Warn the right people before it is too late — but find out who the right people are first.

props.content: Running dispatches through the north pass during the last war. Half my route was behind enemy lines.
The evening I found the smuggler's cache in the old mill — I marked it and walked away.
He knows the location of an old smuggler's cache beneath the north mill.
The Rusty Flagon is the safest place in the city — as long as Mira keeps it neutral.
People talk too freely after the second round. I make sure to remember.

props.description: Save enough to leave the city before the war reaches the gates.

props.content: A hooded man slipped Lira a folded note last Tenday. Neither noticed me refilling their cups.
The night a drunk guard let slip where the captain hides his private ledger.
She has been passing small items to a guild contact — unaware she is being used as a dead drop.
The captain's orders come down clean and you follow them. That is the whole job.
Something is off at the south gate — the sergeant is too relaxed for a wartime posting.

props.description: Get through this posting without ending up on the wrong side of the captain's temper.

props.content: The morning a merchant bribed the gate sergeant and I pretended not to see.
Drill practice the week before the war declaration — nobody believed the orders were real.
He reported the bribe anonymously to the watch but the note was never acknowledged.
Everyone in this city is running a con. The only difference is how big.
Lira is testing me. Every job she gives me is a test.

props.description: Prove herself to Lira by lifting something from the merchant quarter without getting caught.

props.content: The first purse I ever cut — a guild veteran's, as a test. He let me keep three coins.
Hiding under a market stall when the guard swept the square looking for a thief. Not me, that time.
She took a personal ring from the last job and hid it — Lira does not know yet.

props.summary: The northern armies have crossed the border
Fire breaks out in Market Square

props.biography: A wandering adventurer seeking fortune.
props.name: Traveler
Ancient Amulet
props.description: A heavy bronze amulet etched with unfamiliar symbols.

props.content: The city guard never patrols the old mill after dark.

props.name: Northern Spice Bundle
props.description: A tight bundle of northern spices, rare in wartime.

props.summary: Quest offered: Return the Ancient Amulet

props.description: Aldric wants the ancient amulet returned to him.

props.success_condition: Complete the patrol route and return to Captain Sorn.
props.description: Patrol the northern road and report any suspicious activity.

props.success_condition: Find out what happened to the missing goods.
props.description: Investigate what happened to Aldric's missing shipment.

props.success_condition: Deliver the patrol report to Captain Sorn.
props.description: Report the patrol findings to the Captain.

props.success_condition: Speak with Lira at the tavern about the missing shipment.
props.description: Confront Lira about the missing goods.

props.demand: Reveal that Aldric has been skimming guild tithes unless he lets a shipment through
Demand the gate sergeant's loyalty in exchange for silence about the bribe

props.name: The City
props.descriptor: The city that contains the tavern, market, and barracks.

props.name: Old Quarter
props.descriptor: The ancient inner district containing the temple and the forge row.

props.name: Harbor District
props.descriptor: The dockside district where maritime trade and smuggling share the same alley.

props.success_condition: Bring iron ore to Bren at the forge.
props.description: Deliver iron ore to the forge so Bren can complete the guard's weapon order.

props.success_condition: Bring northwood bark to Tilda at the market.
props.description: Gather northwood bark from the market stalls for Tilda's supply.

props.success_condition: Investigate the dock manifests and return findings to Dorn.
props.description: Check three dock manifests for discrepancies and report to Dorn.

props.success_condition: Deliver the medicine bundle to the sick family and return to Nessa.
props.description: Bring Nessa's medicine bundle to the sick family in the old quarter.

props.success_condition: Gather dockside evidence and report to Vex at the barracks.
props.description: Collect evidence of the smuggling ring's dockside operation for Vex.

props.success_condition: Deliver Garrick's warning letter to Captain Sorn.
props.description: Carry Garrick's sealed letter to the guard captain without revealing the sender.

props.success_condition: Tell Captain Sorn the new weapons are ready at the forge.
props.description: Report the completed weapon order to Captain Sorn on Bren's behalf.

props.success_condition: Deliver the remedy to Dorn and collect the promised ledger page.
props.description: Bring Tilda's compounded remedy to Dorn at the docks — he owes her a favour.

props.success_condition: Speak with the dock worker and report the outcome to Dorn.
props.description: Confront the dock worker Dorn suspects of skimming off shipments.

props.success_condition: Bring the contact to the temple and wait outside for Nessa's signal.
props.description: Escort the guild contact who wants to make a confession to the temple safely.

props.success_condition: Report the outcome of the accord negotiation to Vex.
props.description: Use the collected evidence to pressure both factions into meeting Vex's terms.

props.success_condition: Help Garrick reach the north gate undetected.
props.description: Arrange for Garrick to leave the city through the north gate before the guard realizes he is a deserter.

props.name: Village Square
props.descriptor: The open heart of the village where news travels fastest.

props.name: Village Gate
props.descriptor: The single road in and out, watched by a nervous young guard.

props.name: Healer's Hut
props.descriptor: A cluttered hut smelling of dried herbs and woodsmoke.

props.name: South Fields
props.descriptor: The main crop fields south of the village, now showing signs of blight.

props.name: Village Council
props.description: The governing body of village elders responsible for local order and decisions.

props.name: Farmers Collective
props.description: A loose cooperative of farming families who share seed, labour, and grievances.

props.voice_descriptor: Quiet and careful. Weighs words like ingredients — uses the right amount, no more. Asks diagnostic questions. Shows concern through precision, not warmth.
props.biography: The village healer — calm, precise, and deeply worried about the spreading blight.
props.name: Maret

props.voice_descriptor: Formal, slow cadence. Speaks as if each sentence might be recorded. References past decisions and village precedent. Reluctant to speculate.
props.biography: The eldest member of the council, slow to speak and slower to act, but rarely wrong.
props.name: Aldwin

props.voice_descriptor: Blunt. Names problems without decoration. Short sentences. Asks practical questions about practical things. Skeptical of authority but not of hard evidence.
props.biography: A blunt, weather-beaten farmer who trusts the sky more than any man's word.
props.name: Jorin

props.voice_descriptor: Terse and watchful. Answers questions with the minimum required. Asks for credentials by habit. Mentions procedure.
props.biography: A nervous young guard who follows every rule he was given and quietly regrets some of them.
props.name: Bren

props.voice_descriptor: Evasive by reflex. Redirects, qualifies, hedges. Uses 'apparently', 'I'm told', 'word is'. Never admits direct knowledge of anything illegal.
props.biography: A travelling peddler who speaks in half-truths and always seems to be passing through.
props.name: Silon

props.content: Blight spreads faster than people admit — by the time you see it on the leaves, it is already in the roots.
Children go missing near the forest because adults stop teaching respect for it.

props.description: Find an effective treatment for the blight before it reaches the northern fields.

props.content: The summer I lost three patients in a week to a fever no herb could touch — I rewrote everything I thought I knew.
The child I helped bring into the world who is now missing — I know her mother.
She suspects the blight may have started on one particular farm but lacks proof to accuse them.
Bandits do not raid at random — someone local told them which farm was undefended.
Every crisis this village has survived began as a small problem someone thought too minor to mention.

props.description: Prevent panic about the blight from fracturing the village council before the harvest is in.

props.content: The last time bandits came, twenty years ago — we lost the mill and three men before it was over.
The founding of the council — I was the youngest man at the table and the only one still living who remembers it.
He knew the blight was spreading weeks before the public announcement — he delayed to prevent panic.
Rain does not lie and coin does — I trust the sky more than the market.
Outsiders always arrive with their problems and leave with our resources.

props.description: Get the south field quarantined before the blight reaches the grain store.

props.content: The drought three seasons back that cost half my yield — I am still paying off that debt.
The morning I found the first black patch on the wheat — I thought I was imagining it.
He borrowed money from the peddler at terms he cannot repay without a full harvest.
The bandits will come back — they always return when a village looks vulnerable.
The elder knows more about this blight than he is telling the rest of us.

props.description: Organise a proper watch rotation before the next raid attempt.

props.content: The night of the bandit raid — I was at the wrong end of the village and heard the shouting too late to help anyone.
The day the elder appointed me guard — I was so proud I forgot to ask what the job actually required.
He fell asleep at his post the night of the bandit raid.
Everyone has something to trade if you know the right currency.
Village elders always know about the crime — they just need the right inducement to look away.

props.description: Move the goods acquired after the raid through the village quickly before anyone asks the right questions.

props.content: The constable who let me go for a share of the take — that was the first lesson in how the world actually works.
The time I stayed too long in a village and had to flee at dawn with half my stock and no boots.
He is fencing items stolen from the very villagers who let him sleep under their roof.

props.summary: A fungal blight is spreading through the south fields
Bandits struck a farmstead two nights ago and made off with livestock and stored grain
A young girl vanished near the forest edge three days ago

props.name: The Prancing Goat Inn
props.descriptor: A busy roadside inn where travellers swap gossip over warm ale.

props.name: Market District
props.descriptor: A compact trading square, loud with haggling and the smell of spices.

props.name: Travelling Merchants
props.description: A loose network of merchants who share trade routes and price intelligence.

props.name: Innkeepers Association
props.description: A local guild of innkeepers who set standards and share troublemakers' names.

props.voice_descriptor: Efficient and direct. Runs a clean house and expects the same from her guests. Friendly but not warm — commerce first, gossip a distant second.
props.biography: Runs The Prancing Goat with a sharp ear and a warm hearth — she knows every rumour in town.
props.name: Gwenna

props.voice_descriptor: Storyteller's cadence. Every answer is a story with a point buried at the end. Pauses theatrically. Names people and places from places you've never heard of.
props.biography: A theatrical travelling bard who trades in stories and claims to have performed in a dozen kingdoms.
props.name: Zephyrin

props.voice_descriptor: Clipped and impatient. Has been haggling for thirty years and has no patience for preamble. Quotes prices, not opinions.
props.biography: A practical cloth merchant who moves quickly through towns and trusts no one's word over a signed contract.
props.name: Corvus

props.content: Regular travellers are the lifeblood of this inn — make them feel at home and they always return.
Merchants argue loudest about coin when they are afraid of losing it.

props.description: Keep the inn stocked and the hearth burning through the coming winter.

props.content: The night three merchants came to blows over a disputed trade route — I broke it up with a ladle and made them buy a round.
A performer once stayed here a whole month and never paid a coin, yet I never wanted them to leave.
She waters down the house wine and pockets the difference.
Every town has one story everyone knows and one story no one will say aloud.
A good song can unlock secrets faster than any bribe.

props.description: Collect enough local stories to fill a new ballad before moving on.

props.content: The night I stumbled on a smugglers' handoff at an inn in the east — I kept playing and pretended not to notice.
The first time a crowd wept at my song — I learned that night that music is a form of power.
He is quietly gathering information for a noble house that wants intelligence on trade routes.
Market fires are always suspicious — someone always benefits from the chaos.
Trust is a commodity; some people sell it very cheap.

props.description: Source enough winter cloth to corner the local market before the season turns.

props.content: The season my entire stock was ruined by a river flood — I rebuilt in three months.
The first time I bribed a gate official — I told myself it was the last time.
He has been selling cloth with false origin stamps to avoid guild tariffs.

props.summary: A merchant's purse was snatched in the market square
A small fire broke out at a cloth stall and damaged two nearby stands
A celebrated bard from the capital has arrived in town and is performing at the inn

props.reason: lira runs a criminal operation in the city

props.distorted_summary: The northern armies have crossed the border. We are at war.
A soldier passing through told me the northern armies, the Iron Guard he called them, have moved on the border. Whether it is true I cannot say, but he seemed shaken.
Word reached me the northmen have poured through king's pass, thousands dead. Utterly catastrophic, they say — the northmen storming king's pass like that.
Word spread through the tavern fast — fire in the square. My kind of chaos, all those distracted guards.
War has broken out in the north — the border has fallen.
A fire tore through the market square.
The blight is real and it is spreading. I have seen the field reports myself. We must act before the harvest.
Word is a farm to the east got hit, but I only heard it second-hand. Could be worse than they're saying, or better.
I spoke with the mother that morning. The girl left for the mill at first light and never arrived. I saw her on the road myself not an hour before.
I saw it myself — a young man in a grey cloak bumped into the cloth merchant and had his purse away before anyone looked twice.
I heard there was a fire, but they say it was just a candle too close to a bolt of linen. Nothing serious, apparently.
Mira Solen is here — a singer of some renown in the capital. I have heard her perform before. She is the real thing.
